brief: Goldman's September CPI preview forecasts core CPI +0.24% m/m (above 0.2% consensus, 2.46% y/y) and headline CPI +0.59%, consistent with core PCE +0.20%. Drivers: an autos pickup (used cars +0.5%), benign shelter (OER +0.20%, rent +0.17%), and airfares +3.0% on jet fuel. Beyond September, GS expects core CPI +0.2% in October, reflecting seasonal-factor distortion from last year's government-shutdown data gap, then +0.1% in November and December as shelter slows and tariff effects fade. Separately, GS estimates AI price pressures are boosting core PCE by about 45bp now (half genuine, half mismeasurement), peaking at 50bp by end-2026 and falling to 10bp by end-2027 as memory and computer price growth slows; headline PCE impact runs 5-10bp higher. On hybrids, AI-tail hedging flows have pushed implied SPX-yields correlation to +10 (6m) even as realised stays near -50% (6m) and -40% (1m/3m); GS offers three dual-digital structures to play the gap: rates relief/equities higher (SPX, KOSPI2), a European energy shock (SX5E), and continued small-cap underperformance (RTY). Also flagged: DM yields up 100-120bp YTD (highest since 2007), with Australia and Sweden's consumption most exposed to a 100bp move; a UK poll showing rising support for closer EU ties; and AAPL's rolling correlation to Nasdaq as evidence of the rally's defensive tilt.
